title: ZPA App Connector, group, schedule and version profile calls: what is sent and where the sources differ

prose.text: This is the wire behavior of the App Connector schedule, group, connector and version profile calls that field listings do not show: which tags drop or force values, where the SDKs disagree, and what the OpenAPI document does not list. Field names and types come from the surface layer (`node scripts/kb.mjs surface`) and the group's behavior from [[zpa.app-connectors.connector-groups]].
{{schedule-singleton}} {{schedule-frequency-days}} The interval check and the refusal to update a disabled schedule are in [[zpa.sdk-go.service-defects]] and [[zpa.terraform.resource-fidelity]].
{{schedule-update-path}} Whether the API accepts that update is open {{gap:schedule-put-undocumented}}.

{{version-profile-reads}} {{version-profile-names}} {{version-profile-gid-key}} {{python-version-profile-gid-unread}} The two SDKs use different wire keys for it {{divergence:version-profile-gid-wire-key}}.
{{python-version-profile-slugs}} The key reaches the wire camel-cased as `versionProfile`; what the server does with it is open {{gap:python-version-profile-wire}}.
The type of the interval differs between the contract and the Go SDK {{divergence:schedule-frequency-interval-type}}.
The id type of the bulk-delete body differs between contract and SDKs {{divergence:bulk-delete-id-type}}.
The upgrade attempt counter has different types in the contract and the Go structs {{divergence:upgrade-attempt-type}}.
The Python model defaults a missing enabled to true: {{python-connector-enabled-default}}
Whether frequencies other than days are accepted is open {{gap:frequency-values}}.

checks.do: Whether a schedule update failed before any request (a disabled or invalid-interval schedule) or at the API, and whether the PUT path is documented.
Whether a group's boolean is false in the tenant because it was sent that way on a write.
Which version profile an override group is using, and which SDK wrote it, before trusting a slug passed to the Python group methods.
Whether a connector list used sort parameters that only the connector endpoint accepts.

schedule-singleton.statement: The Go SDK decodes GET on the App Connector schedule endpoint into a single schedule object, not a list, and creates it with POST; the OpenAPI document describes the same two operations on connectorSchedule, with POST answering 204 No Content.

schedule-update-path.statement: The Go SDK updates the App Connector schedule with PUT to the connectorSchedule endpoint followed by the schedule ID and expects no response body.
schedule-update-path.conditions: The OpenAPI document lists only GET and POST under connectorSchedule and a PUT only under serviceEdgeSchedule/{id}; see the gap schedule-put-undocumented.

schedule-frequency-days.statement: The Terraform provider's App Connector assistant schedule resource accepts only `days` for `frequency`.

schedule-create-already-exists.statement: The Go SDK schedule integration test treats a CreateSchedule error containing `resource.already.exist` as the schedule already being enabled rather than as a failure, and accepts status 200 or 204 on success.

group-booleans-always-sent.statement: The Go App Connector group request tags `enabled`, `overrideVersionProfile`, `praEnabled`, `wafDisabled`, `tcpQuickAckApp`, `tcpQuickAckAssistant`, `useInDrMode`, `tcpQuickAckReadAssistant` and `lssAppConnectorGroup` without omitempty, and so are `cityCountry` and `dcHostingInfo`, so false and empty values are sent on every write.
group-booleans-always-sent.conditions: Group `enabled` and `overrideVersionProfile` are the fields the provider writes from state; the zero-value effect is in shared.sdk-go.zero-value-writes.

group-server-groups-key.statement: On the Go App Connector group the field `AppServerGroup` is sent under the key `serverGroups`, and the Python App Connector controller maps `server_group_ids` to `serverGroups`.

connector-no-create.statement: The Go appconnectorcontroller package exposes Get, GetByName, GetAll, Update, Delete and BulkDelete and no Create function.

quotes: func Get(ctx context.Context, service *zscaler.Service, appConnectorID string)
func GetByName(ctx context.Context, service *zscaler.Service, appConnectorName string)
func Update(ctx context.Context, service *zscaler.Service, appConnectorID string, appConnector AppConnector)
func Delete(ctx context.Context, service *zscaler.Service, appConnectorID string)

connector-no-create.conditions: The absence of a Create function is shown by a grep of `^func ` in the file at the pin.

connector-write-tags.statement: The Go App Connector request tags `enabled` omitempty, so false is not sent, but tags `provisioningKeyId` and `provisioningKeyName` without omitempty, so both are always sent; the group's `enabled` is the opposite.

connector-sub-module-key.statement: The Go App Connector maps its `ZPNSubModuleUpgrade` field to the JSON key `zpnSubModuleUpgradeList`, and holds `enrollmentCert` as an unstructured map.

version-profile-gid-key.statement: Inside a version profile's `versions` entries the Go SDK tags the profile reference `version_profile_gid`, in snake case, while the sibling fields are camel case. The Python ComponentLevelVersion model (the `version` object of a connector or connector group) looks up and emits the same `version_profile_gid` key, but the Python client camel-cases every response key before a model reads it.

quotes: self.version_profile_gid = config["version_profile_gid"] if "version_profile_gid" in config else None

version-profile-gid-key.conditions: Statement changed per verifier: it said the Python model reads and writes the key as Go does, but form_response_body renames response keys before the model sees them. models/common.py holds an identical ComponentLevelVersion that no module imports. The consequence for Python reads and writes is the claim python-version-profile-gid-unread.

python-version-profile-gid-unread.statement: A Python connector or connector group read never finds a `version_profile_gid` key, because the response key arrives as `versionProfileGid`, so the model's `version_profile_gid` is always None; and a `version_profile_gid` key in a Python request body is sent as `versionProfileGid`, the key Go does not use.
python-version-profile-gid-unread.conditions: Follows from form_response_body camel-casing every key with to_lower_camel_case, which has no exception for version_profile_gid, and from the executor converting request bodies the same way. Which key the server sends and accepts is not shown: the OpenAPI document has no version_profile_gid or versionProfileGid.

version-profile-reads.statement: The Go SDK lists version profiles from `/visible/versionProfiles` and finds one by name with a case-insensitive match; the Python SDK reads the profile associated with the customer from `/versionProfile`; the OpenAPI document has GET operations on both paths.

version-profile-names.statement: The Go version profile integration test requires the names `New Release`, `Default`, `Previous Default` and `Default - el8` to be present, and the App Connector group test pairs `Default` with version profile ID `0`.

python-version-profile-slugs.statement: The Python helper `pick_version_profile` converts the slugs `default`, `previous_default` and `new_release` to version profile IDs 0, 1 and 2 and sets `overrideVersionProfile`, but the App Connector group add and update methods pass their keyword arguments as the request body without calling it.

evidence.note: the module imports only format_url from zscaler.utils, so pick_version_profile is not called here

python-version-profile-slugs.conditions: pick_version_profile has no caller anywhere under zscaler/ at the pin (grep). The group docstrings still document `version_profile` with the three slugs as accepted values. The executor camel-cases the request body, so a `version_profile` keyword reaches the wire as `versionProfile`; what the server does with that key is not shown.

version-profile-put.statement: The Go SDK `Update` for version profiles sends a PUT to `/visible/versionProfiles/{id}` carrying the whole profile object.

python-version-profile-put.statement: The Python SDK `update_version_profile` sends a PUT to `/versionProfiles/{id}` with a body of only `removeOverrideFlag`, and expects 204 No Content.

quotes: Note: This API returns 204 No Content on success, so the result will be None.

group-sub-resources.statement: The Go SDK reads the App Connector group summary from `appConnectorGroup/summary`, decoded as id, name and enabled only, and reads one group with its server groups from `appConnectorGroup/{id}/sg` as a full group.

quotes: type CommonSummary struct { ID string `json:"id,omitempty"` Name string `json:"name,omitempty"` Enabled bool `json:"enabled,omitempty"` }

list-params.statement: The OpenAPI connector list takes search, page, pagesize, sortBy, sortDir and microtenantId, with a default page size of 20 and a maximum of 500; the App Connector group list takes the same paging parameters but scopeId instead of sort parameters.

expect.description: Specifies the page size. If not provided, the default page size is 20. The max page size is 500.
Indicates the parameter to sort by.
Specifies the page size. If not provided, the default page size is 20. The max page size is 500.

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the ZPA tenant.
parameters.name: customerId

parameters.description: The search string used to support search by features and fields for the API.
parameters.name: search

parameters.description: Specifies the page size. If not provided, the default page size is 20. The max page size is 500.
parameters.name: pagesize

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the microtenant of ZPA tenant. For Default microtenant 0 should be passed and for Customer data microtenant should be null.
parameters.name: microtenantId

evidence.note: the group list's complete parameters: customerId, search, page, pagesize, scopeId, microtenantId; no sortBy or sortDir

list-params.conditions: The absence of sortBy on the group list is read from its parameter list in the OpenAPI document. The Go SDK's own default page size is covered in shared.sdk-go.list-pagination.

python-connector-enabled-default.statement: The Python App Connector model reads `enabled` as True when the response carries no `enabled` key.

quotes: self.enabled = config["enabled"] if "enabled" in config else True

version-profile-gid-wire-key.summary: The wire key of the version profile reference: the Go SDK uses snake-case `version_profile_gid`, while the Python client renames every key to camel case, so it sends `versionProfileGid` and cannot read `version_profile_gid`.

positions.says: The Go version profile `versions` entry tags the reference `version_profile_gid`.
The Python client camel-cases every response key before a model reads it, so the model's `version_profile_gid` lookup finds nothing.
The Python executor camel-cases request-body keys, so a `version_profile_gid` key is sent as `versionProfileGid`.

evidence.after: # Preserve existing logic for other services

version-profile-gid-wire-key.impact: If the server uses the Go spelling, Python callers never see a connector's or group's version profile GID and cannot send it under that key. The OpenAPI document names neither key, so which spelling the server uses is not shown; read a raw response to check.

version-profile-put-path.summary: Which path a version profile update goes to

positions.says: The Go SDK updates a version profile with PUT on /visible/versionProfiles/{id}.
The Python SDK updates it with PUT on /versionProfiles/{id}, sending only removeOverrideFlag.

version-profile-put-path.impact: The two SDKs write to different paths with different bodies, and the OpenAPI document lists no PUT for either path. A version profile update through one SDK says nothing about the other; confirm the effect by reading the group's version profile back.

schedule-frequency-interval-type.summary: The OpenAPI document types a schedule's `frequencyInterval` as an int32 integer, while the Go SDK types it as a string and validates it against string keys.

positions.says: The contract request body for POST connectorSchedule has frequencyInterval as an int32 integer.
The Go schedule struct declares FrequencyInterval as a string.
The Go update check accepts only the string keys 5, 7, 14, 30, 60 and 90; create sends the value unchecked.

quotes: func UpdateSchedule(ctx context.Context, service *zscaler.Service, schedulerID string
validIntervals := map[string]bool{"5": true, "7": true, "14": true, "30": true, "60": true, "90": true}

positions.says: The Python SDK passes frequency_interval through as supplied.

schedule-frequency-interval-type.impact: A caller following the contract sends a number and one following the Go SDK sends a numeric string. The Go integration test sends the string form; no captured run shows whether the API accepts the string, the number, or both.

bulk-delete-id-type.summary: The OpenAPI document types the connector bulk-delete `ids` as int64 integers, while the Go request holds them as strings and the Python SDK examples pass strings.

positions.says: The contract request body for connector/bulkDelete has ids as an array of int64 integers.
The Go BulkDeleteRequest holds IDs as a list of strings.
The Python bulk_delete_connectors sends the caller's list under ids and documents string IDs.

bulk-delete-id-type.impact: Raw-HTTP callers follow the contract and send numbers; both SDKs send numeric strings. Whether the API accepts both forms is not shown.

upgrade-attempt-type.summary: The OpenAPI document types a connector's read-only `upgradeAttempt` as an int32 integer, while the Go SDK types it as a string in its connector structs.

positions.says: The contract connector item in an App Connector Group response has upgradeAttempt as a read-only int32.
The Go AppConnector type (used for an App Connector Group's connectors) declares UpgradeAttempt as a string.
The Go servergroup Connectors type (a server group's connector groups' connectors) also declares UpgradeAttempt as a string.

upgrade-attempt-type.impact: A Go caller decoding a bare JSON integer into a string field gets a decode error rather than a value; the live response is not captured.

schedule-put-undocumented.title: Whether the API accepts PUT on the App Connector schedule with an ID
schedule-put-undocumented.blocks: telling whether the SDK update path calls a real endpoint
schedule-put-undocumented.detail: Unverified legacy statement: the legacy reference records PUT for the App Connector schedule update. The Go SDK sends PUT to connectorSchedule/{id}, but the OpenAPI document lists only GET and POST under connectorSchedule and a PUT only under serviceEdgeSchedule/{id}. The Go SDK's own integration test expects a 200 from that PUT; that is the test's assertion, not a recorded result. In a scratch tenant, send the update and record the status and the schedule afterwards.

quotes: updateResp, err := UpdateSchedule(ctx, service, schedule.ID, schedule)

python-version-profile-wire.title: What the API does with the versionProfile key the Python group methods send
python-version-profile-wire.blocks: telling whether Python callers can set a group's version profile by slug
python-version-profile-wire.detail: Unverified legacy statement: the legacy reference says the Python slugs 'map to IDs at the API layer'. The only slug-to-ID mapping in the SDK is an uncalled helper. The executor camel-cases the request body, so a `version_profile` keyword reaches the wire as `versionProfile`, not as the raw snake-case key. Create a group with version_profile set and read the group's versionProfileId back.

frequency-values.title: Which frequency values the schedule endpoints accept besides days
frequency-values.detail: The Terraform provider allows only `days` for frequency on both the App Connector and the Service Edge assistant schedule resources ([[zpa.api.app-connectors-wire:schedule-frequency-days]]), and the Go SDK test uses days. The OpenAPI document types frequency as a plain string with no enum. A client-side restriction does not settle what the API accepts, so whether it takes other values is still open. Send a schedule with another value in a scratch tenant and record the result.
frequency-values.blocks: telling whether hours or weeks are valid schedule frequencies
